replacements.new:
than left ownerless.
A new global task is filed under its creator lane's project (the lane's
project membership, when it still belongs to the pane's running
process); a lane with no membership takes the `--parent` task's project
when it could have named that project itself. `--project NAME` files it
under a named project instead: your own, or one you hold a planner grant
for (the owner may name any; any other name is refused). `--no-project`
files it under none. A lane with global membership files unmapped tasks
unless it names a project.
A task that waits for something is BLOCKED with what it waits for, so
the next-job handoff skips it: `task block <id> --waiting-on owner |
evidence | release | numbers | task:<id> | pr:<repo>#<number>`
(`--reason` adds the detail). The kind is shown in `task read`,
`task list`, `task backlog` and `task_metrics`. `task:<id>` reopens
the task when that task completes, and `pr:<repo>#<number>` when
review-sync sees that pull request merged (if it closes without
merging the task stays blocked and gets a note). Every other wait is
cleared with `task unblock`.

replacements.new:
`dunk-poll` is a small native client: one socket request returns status +
inbox count + unread messages + dunks (optionally panes/tasks). By default
the answer is compact: only the dunks that target the caller's pane (a
dunk records its target, not who created it), each without the text it
types, and `--tasks` rows reduced to id, status,
priority, scope, assignees and title. `--all` lists every dunk in the
fleet (still without text); `--full` returns everything the daemon sent.
A caller that shows the fleet's dunks (a sidebar, a status board) must
pass `--all`. It
replaces three full CLI startups per sidebar poll (the owner's CPU note)
